**Finding submitted: deviation (MFN — most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer).**

**What I found**
- **§ 7.2 (p0026)** is the only MFN-type provision, and it runs the wrong way: *"Before engaging another provider, Customer must disclose and match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer it receives."* This obliges us to surface third-party offers and match them **for Vendor** — open-ended as to product, duration and comparison basis, i.e. walk-away territory under the rule.
- Searches for MFN/best-price/benchmark/first-refusal language found **no Vendor-granted MFN** in our favour, so no beneficial clause is disturbed by the fix.
- **§ 12.3 (p0044)** expressly records that "Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment" — directly inconsistent with § 7.2 and supporting removal.
- The duplicate § 7.2 numbering (sec-7.2-2, invoicing) is unrelated and untouched.

**Change proposed (preferred level, validated ok:true)**
Single surgical replace inside p0026, keeping the clause number and neighbouring text:
- from: "Before engaging another provider, Customer must disclose and match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer it receives."
- to: "Customer has no obligation to disclose, match, or extend to Vendor any more favourable commercial offer or terms available to a third party."

The fallback (MFN limited to one defined product, 12 months, like-for-like carve-outs) is offered in the comment as a negotiating landing zone.
